subject: frostAxe
pitch:
Category: Fantasy weapon.
Subject: frost-forged battle axe.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TS module for a frost-forged battle axe, League of Legends style, with a root joint even though it's a non-creature prop, standing upright on a small icy rock plinth base.

I'm sketching the parts: an octagonal stone base with snow and ice crystal cones, a vertical haft with leather-wrap torus bands planted into the stone, and an asymmetric double-ended head with a large crescent main blade on one side and a spike/smaller blade plus glowing crystal on the other, all extruded flat with thickness along the local axis.

Defining the crescent blade outline...

Now I'm thinking about adding a glowing rune inlay with a frost snowflake emblem, using a separate thin plane textured with SVG carved lines placed just in front of each blade face.

For the back blade, I'm shaping a mirrored, smaller fluked spike profile plus an upward ice crystal spike, then designing the head socket as a collar with blued frost-steel and gilt ornamental ring bands to match the gold-and-cyan theme.

Now I'm adding a glowing cyan octahedron gem with a gold bezel on the collar front, plus angled ice crystal cones sprouting from the head and small frost spikes along the blade edge. For the grip, I'm layering flat torus leather wrap bands and sweeping a flat ribbon tassel along a bezier path below the head for a swaying cel-shaded accent.

For the base, I'm lathing an octagonal stone plinth with mottled gray paint and a snow-dusted top, surrounding it with hexagonal frost crystal cones and spiky shards rotated outward, plus a few snow mound spheres. I'm considering a flat glowing rune circle texture on the plinth top, then setting the overall axe proportions (haft, head, spike) for a heroic ~1.75 unit height, and defining the root joint before assigning bone parenting for all parts.

I'm sweeping a tapered haft shape with grain texture, adding a glowing octahedron ice gem accent, and writing a cone helper function to generate directional ice crystal spikes with computed centers from base and direction vectors, along with their color palette.

For the blade, I'm positioning a transparent rune-inlay plane with crescent and snowflake line art on the face, making it glow, and working out the thin blade thickness so the faces sit symmetrically around center.

I'll keep the snowflake emblem on the blade only, skip a collar gem/bezel idea, and add a simple rune circle texture on the base top plus squashed spheres for snow. Then I'll add a thin edge highlight along the blade.

I'm placing small ice-crystal cones jutting from the blade's spine near the collar top, with a gilt cap cone at the collar's bottom end, and sketching out a lateral flange plate where the blade meets the collar.

Shaping a narrow gilt bracket outline...

Defining hammer/fluke outline points...

Writing blade paint function...

Now I'm sketching a ribbon swept along a bezier curve with a tapering box section in blue, threading past the haft, with a gem knot at the start and a gilt tassel cone at the end.

Still writing geometry...

Placing the gem as an octahedron at the top with a gilt torus bezel and collar, then adding blued cylinder collars with gilt end rings along the haft. That covers the ornamentation, so I'm ready to write the final code.
